The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Former NYSE president says stock issuers hold the key to tokenization as Bullish builds its platform. Stacey Cunningham, who recently joined digital asset platform Bullish as President, sees the company’s planned Equiniti acquisition and focus on stock issuers as key to its tokenization ambitions. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Goldman Sachs, Citi among banks said to commit $270 million to stablecoin venture. The venture, known as Project Faro, plans to issue a dollar-denominated stablecoin and is expected to be incorporated in the U.S. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto is now teamed up with U.S. government in two legal battles over perps. Twice now, crypto firms have found themselves on the side of the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission in holding that perpetual futures aren't swaps. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Plume affiliate lands broker-dealer license to bring real U.S. assets onchain. Kimber Digital Securities secured SEC and Finra approvals, a regulatory milestone paving the way for the delivery of legally binding claims, dividends, and yield-bearing products directly to self-custodial wallets and stablecoin applications in the U.S. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Will stablecoins survive once the banks catch up?. As crypto firms and banks converge, it is fair to ask what lasting advantage stablecoins have, argues Alessandro Hatami, founder of Pacemakers and former COO of Digital Banking at Lloyds Banking Group. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

U.S. CPI rose stronger than expected 0.4% in October; core rate rose 0.3%. A December rate hike appears completely assured, with Fed Governor Chris Waller suggesting even a 50-basis-point move could be appropriate. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $73,603 with a -1.39% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,050.17 with a -3.57% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Crypto ETFs End 8-Week Outflow Streak With $282M Inflows as Bitcoin and Ethereum Demand Rebounds
items.description:
After two months of relentless selling pressure, cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have finally posted their first week of positive flows, signaling a potential improvement in institutional sentiment toward digital assets.

Global crypto investment products attracted $281.8 million in net inflows last week, ending an eight-week stretch of outflows that erased more than $7 billion from the sector. [...] Daily flows reflected continued uncertainty among investors. Funds attracted more than $265 million on July 6, the strongest single-day inflow since early May, before sharply slowing the following day.

The middle of the week saw renewed outflows before demand recovered again on Friday with another positive session.

Despite the improvement, the latest inflows remain small compared with the more than $8 billion that exited Bitcoin ETFs over the previous eight weeks. [...] US-listed spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $197.4 million in net inflows during the week ending July 10, breaking an eight-week streak of outflows that had persisted since the second week of May.

The weekly figure was driven primarily by BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), which continued to dominate the market.

IBIT attracted nearly $292 million during the week, offsetting significant withdrawals from Grayscale's GBTC, Fidelity's FBTC, and ARK 21Shares' Bitcoin ETF.

items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established the first federal regulatory framework for stablecoins in the United States. It limits who can issue stablecoins and requires issuers to maintain reserves backing the tokens they have issued, make monthly disclosures detailing the assets held in reserve, and comply with anti–money laundering and consumer protection requirements.

### What is the CLARITY Act? [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight.

items.title: Geopolitical risk, US–China tensions, and systemic risk in cryptocurrency markets: A regime-dependent analysis
items.description: Cryptocurrency markets have become increasingly integrated into the global financial system, yet their systemic vulnerabilities to geopolitical shocks remain poorly understood. This paper provides the first empirical analysis linking US–China tensions (UCT) to systemic risk in cryptocurrency markets. Using monthly data from August 2015 to February 2024, we measure systemic interconnectedness via a TVP-VAR Total Connectedness Index, applying linear and nonlinear ARDL frameworks to the full [...] to the full sample, as well as to bearish and bullish markets separately. The results reveal strong persistence in systemic risk. Crucially, UCT emerges as the dominant driver of contagion across all regimes, whereas general geopolitical risk (GPR) measures exhibit limited explanatory power. The nonlinear analysis uncovers symmetric long-run effects, indicating that the mere uncertainty of UCT, whether increasing or decreasing, elevates long-run systemic risk. Furthermore, lagged Bitcoin [...] lagged Bitcoin trading volume consistently exacerbates contagion across all regimes. These findings provide implications for regulators and investors, highlighting the necessity for regime-sensitive, geopolitically informed risk management strategies.
